title: Vacuum breaker installation starts with pressure condition, hazard, and height
description: Choose hose-connection, atmospheric, or pressure vacuum protection by application instead of treating every air-inlet device as interchangeable.
answer: The device must match backsiphonage risk, continuous versus non-continuous pressure, downstream valves, elevation, testability, and the local authority's accepted method.
urgency: A wrong device or wrong height can appear functional while failing the required protection. Use local code and product instructions.
diagramAlt: Vacuum breaker type selector showing hose connection, AVB, and elevated PVB
identifiers: Hose-connection devices mount at the faucet.
AVBs need the correct non-continuous pressure arrangement.
PVBs are elevated testable assemblies for applicable backsiphonage conditions.

choices.label: Outdoor hose faucet
choices.detail: Use the hose-connection device and thread path.

choices.label: Non-continuous irrigation zone
choices.detail: Check AVB height and downstream-valve limits.

choices.label: Testable irrigation assembly
choices.detail: Check PVB elevation, freeze exposure, and testing rule.

steps.title: Define the hazard and pressure
steps.body: Backpressure and continuous pressure can disqualify simpler devices.

steps.title: Use the critical-level requirement
steps.body: Measure from the required downstream point using the listed product marking.

steps.title: Plan testing and winterization
steps.body: Access, drainage, freeze exposure, and utility rules affect the final layout.

safeChecks: Check official local requirements before purchase.
stopConditions: The correct height cannot be achieved
A regulated testable assembly is required
notThisDevice: A vacuum breaker is not suitable for every backflow hazard.
A check valve alone may not satisfy potable protection rules.
A pressure regulator performs a different function.
evidenceNote: The local authority and the listed product instructions determine acceptable type, height, testing, and installation.
